acceptance_condition: For each candidate aggregation operator, a deterministic test (e.g., permuting input order, duplicating an input) establishes whether outputs are invariant (commutative/idempotent) or not, with effect sizes on final-answer variability reported for at least the operators used in the note's experiment.
rationale: Shapiro's theorems give convergence only when merge is a semilattice LUB or updates commute (pages 5–6). Both focal baselines (independent sampling + aggregation, staged Q/A) end in an aggregation step; if that step is a stochastic LLM call, it violates these conditions, so final answers may depend on agent ordering and sampling noise — a confound for the preregistered matched-compute experiment and a mechanistic distinction between aggregation designs.
text: Which aggregation operators used in multi-agent LLM pipelines (majority vote, evidence union, LLM free-text synthesis) satisfy or violate the CRDT sufficient conditions for well-defined merging (commutativity, idempotence, monotonicity), and does order/non-determinism of the final aggregation step measurably change the merged answer?
